verdict.headline: US strikes on Iran push oil to a six-week high and finally crack the stock market
verdict.label: STEP ASIDE — 2 of 4 regime triggers breached: Brent $94.65 and WTI $90.22 (both above oil thresholds) after CENTCOM struck IRGC sites at noon ET. S&P 500 lost 7,650 to close at 7,631.47 (-0.71%), Nasdaq -1.03%, Russell 2000 -1.23%. ISM Manufacturing 54.6; Prices Index 71.1; JOLTS 7.271M; September hike odds 68%; 10Y 4.79%, 30Y 5.28%; gold -1.86%.
verdict.rationale_short: Oil is transmitting to equities through the discount rate rather than the earnings line: ISM showed demand cooling to 53.7 new orders while input prices held at 71.1, so a supply shock now argues for tighter policy instead of easier. Equities absorbed nine sessions of that repricing without flinching and then took it in one afternoon, led from the long-duration end. Two supertankers were struck near the Strait of Hormuz, CENTCOM responded with strikes on IRGC air-defence, radar and mine-laying sites, and Brent settled at $94.65 — the first close above $92 in six weeks. A Brent close back under $90 or a 30-year close under 5.15% dissolves the frame; Brent above $100 with the 30-year settling above 5.30% extends it. Payrolls Friday is the binary: sub-150K unwinds the September hike bet; 200K+ gives Warsh's Fed cover to act.

supporting_data.label: CENTCOM struck IRGC air-defence, radar, naval and mine-laying sites at noon ET after two supertankers were hit near the Strait of Hormuz
Brent settled $4.16 higher at $94.65 (+4.6%), highest since July 24; WTI settled up $4.46 at $90.22 (+5.2%), highest since July 23
September hike odds 68% on CME FedWatch, more than double pre-Jackson Hole level of ~36%
ISM Manufacturing 54.6 versus 55.6 in July; Prices Index unchanged at 71.1 while New Orders fell three points to 53.7
JOLTS openings 7.271M in July, below the 7.33-7.36M consensus; June revised down 177,000 to 7.182M
Dell +9% AH on AI server beat and raised guidance; GitLab +20% AH on Q2 beat; MongoDB -12% AH despite beat
Anthropic signed a six-year, $35B cloud deal with Nvidia-backed Lambda; Nvidia holds the Texas data-centre lease

watchlist_mentions.note: WTI settled at $90.22 (+5.2%), first close above $90 since July 23. Two supertanker strikes in two days; voluntary operator transit suspensions are the next escalation trigger worth watching.
Gold fell 1.86% to $4,358.74, a third consecutive decline into an escalating conflict — the clearest cross-asset signal that the tape is pricing inflation rather than fear.

Down roughly 1% as Anthropic's $35B six-year deal with Lambda left Nvidia as chip supplier, equity holder in both counterparties, and lessee of the Texas data centre. The question raised is financing circularity, not demand.
Fell 2.36% to $459.61 with the semis, on discount-rate pressure rather than company news; a 30-year close back under 5.25% is what unwinds the group's derating.

Fell to ~$76,762 on the strikes, with roughly $115M of long liquidations inside an hour. The $76,661 support is now at the price rather than below it — a sustained close under that level would be the next technical break.

Jumped ~9% after hours after beating on both lines and raising fiscal 2027 guidance on AI server demand. Opens Wednesday as a tell on market appetite for AI-infrastructure beats in a rising-rate tape.

trade_setups.thesis: The long bond has been above 5.30% intraday twice and closed at 5.28% in both sessions, refusing to confirm the level. Treasury buyback operations beginning September 9 are the structural bid against the oil-inflation input. The 30Y closing above 5.30% marks the regime breach that the framework requires.
trade_setups.entry: A daily close above 5.30% is the trigger; a close back under 5.15% says the buyback bid is absorbing supply at the long end
trade_setups.invalidation: Brent back under $90 or a payrolls print under 150K removes the inflation impulse driving the move
trade_setups.horizon: This week, with the September 4 jobs report the decisive test

trade_setups.thesis: Two supertankers have been hit and US forces have struck the mine-laying capability behind it, yet crude is still transiting Hormuz. The distinction that matters is between headline escalation and measured supply disruption — transit behaviour, not strike counts, marks the difference.
trade_setups.entry: Voluntary transit suspensions by major operators put $100 in play; a return under $90 says the premium is decaying on July's schedule
trade_setups.invalidation: A confirmed halt in hostilities or Gulf mediation collapses the risk premium built over three sessions
trade_setups.horizon: Days; Iran's response cadence has tracked 24-36 hour cycles

trade_setups.thesis: The index lost 7,650 in one afternoon after absorbing nine sessions of the same rate move, and the adjustment came from the long-duration end — Nasdaq -1.03% and Russell -1.23% against the Dow's -0.79%. The VIX ended at 16.0 after closing under 15 on August 31, so an event premium now exists where there was none.
trade_setups.entry: Holding 7,580 through Thursday says one afternoon completed the adjustment; losing 7,550 says multiples are still repricing into payrolls
trade_setups.invalidation: A reclaim of 7,700 on softer oil or de-escalation news returns the tape to its pre-strike range

bear_case: The read treats a war-risk premium as an inflation regime. Brent at $94.65 is only its highest since July 24 and WTI at $90.22 its highest since July 23 — a retest of summer levels, not a breakout, and every escalation premium this year has decayed within days of the last strike. The growth evidence cuts against the read as well: ISM at 54.6 is the eighth consecutive month of expansion, and a labour market whose openings were revised down 177,000 will not sustain 68% hike odds through a soft payrolls print. If Brent closes back under $90 and the S&P reclaims 7,700, this read no longer holds.
